il_j_waterfall_west_right.blurb: A small sport wall on Fountain Bluff, south of Gorham above the Mississippi, sitting just right of the waterfall. Thirteen routes, nearly all bolted, mix pockets, bulges and roofs, and a few lines begin from a ledge well off the ground, so expect some committing starts. The grades lean hard: a lone 5.9 and a couple of 5.10s, then a thick middle of 5.12s, with a 5.13 and a 5.14 for the strong. A single trad line is mixed in. It suits a climber with a few seasons of 5.11 and 5.12 behind them rather than a beginner.

il_breaking_bread_cliffline.blurb: A bouldering cliffline in the Hagler Road zone of the Holy Boulders complex in southern Illinois, reached by heading uphill past the big roof; it is the first cluster you meet on the northern stretch. Thirteen problems on good-quality stone, running from V0 warm-ups through a solid block of V1 to V3, with a few V4s, and a pair of hard technical lines at V6 and V7. Moderates dominate, which makes it a decent stop for a mixed-ability group, and there is some talk of more face and slab potential. No sun or shade details are recorded.

il_d_best_in_show_boulder.blurb: An overhanging sandstone block, shaped a bit like a ship, in the House Boulders cluster near the Holy Boulders in southern Illinois. It is among the first boulders reached on the trail from the north, a short way downhill from a fin-shaped boulder. Thirteen problems, all on steep rock, begin around V2 and V3 and climb quickly through V4 to V6 into a stack of very hard testpieces from V8 to V10. This is a destination for strong boulderers rather than a place to warm up, though a couple of easier lines exist. The hillside setting is wooded.

il_l_sunset_corner.blurb: A sector of Fountain Bluff near Gorham, Illinois, a short stroll past the Five Twelve Wall from the waterfall. It has a tall, steep wall alongside slabs and roof pulls, with thirteen climbs: twelve bolted lines and one boulder traverse. Grades start at 5.7, with a few 5.9 to 5.11 routes, then cluster at 5.12 and reach 5.13 on two lines. Good for a climber who has outgrown the easy stuff; sun exposure is not recorded.

il_i_railroad_rock.blurb: A sport crag at the far end of North Canyon in Jackson Falls, in Shawnee National Forest, southern Illinois. It is a long walk by canyon standards, following the old railroad grade or the clifftop trail with a short scramble. The reward is some of the canyon's best climbing on a mostly shaded wall that can stay damp. Twelve bolted routes: a single 5.8, one 5.10, then a block of 5.11s and 5.12s, topping out around 5.12. Not a spot for beginners, and a dry spell helps.

il_c_rainy_day_roof.blurb: A roofed wall at the east end of Jackson Falls canyon in southern Illinois, reached by dropping down the dog walk, turning left down the canyon past the Manky Alcove and Dolphin Rock, then rounding a corner to the right. Twelve routes, mostly bolted with a couple of trad or top-rope lines, running from an easy 5.6 through a handful of 5.9s and 5.10s up to 5.11. The style is technical footwork and compression moves on interesting holds under the roof. A friendly place for a climber moving from 5.9 into 5.10, with several well-liked classics.
